Where I got to
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt — 348 of 349 files byte-identical against their recorded SHA-256 (the exception is export.sh, which contains the dump's own # FILE: banner as literal text and can't be round-tripped by any parser using that banner as a delimiter; it is excluded from the work set rather than reconstructed and guessed at).

I have not yet produced the archive. I hit the tool ceiling during survey. Here is what the survey found, because two of the three items are worth acting on before any code moves.

The §18 check: predicted 1149, observed 1151 — and I can account for both numbers exactly
claude-terminal.txt shows the suite green: total: 1151, failed: 0, succeeded: 1151, skipped: 0, twice (dotnet test and ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e), plus 17/17 end-to-end. Three slices of predictions finally met a run.

The arithmetic:

[Fact] + [InlineData] across the tree = 1132
SchemaMigrationRunnerTests.KeyRelations = 13 theory rows
SchemaMigrationRunnerTests.KeyColumnsAddedByAlter = 6 theory rows
1132 − 5 (its own [Fact]s already counted) + 5 + 13 + 6 = 1151. Substitute 4 for that six and you get 1149 — the predicted number, to the unit.

That is a finding, and it is F-77's shape inside the one section that exists to prevent it. §16.4 says "Four theory rows therefore name the columns that arrived by ALTER". That sentence was true of 0004. 0005 added menu_item.menu_section_identifier and menu_item_event.new_menu_section_identifier to the same TheoryData, and the sentence did not move. TestingSectionContractTests could not catch it: that gate compares assertion counts per class — 7 methods, which is still correct — and a theory-row count is not a method count. So the prediction was derived from prose the gate is structurally blind to.

Per F-77 the repair is to delete the number, not correct it — the rows are derivable from the tree, and this is the second time this exact sentence has gone stale.

A second stale count, same mechanism, one file over
Scenario 16's arithmetic comment says "Fifteen controls are expected … a rename and a reprice on the item". ManageMenuItem.razor carries four .manage-inline-form blocks, not two — Slice 38 added the position form and the comment did not move. Counting the tree: indexes contribute 5 .record-actions + 3 .page-head-action + 3 .filter-actions; details contribute 2 + 1 + 2 + 4 .manage-inline-form plus one .page-head-action on the display roster. The floor of 14 is met either way, which is why nothing reported it — a floor that passes at 15 also passes at 17.

The menu work I had scoped and was about to write
M6 Slice 43 — MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, the last verb in the whole enhancement with no surface. Concretely:

MenuAdministration.cs — the verb, one transaction: lock the item (its LockMenuItemSql and MenuItemLockRow need menu_section_identifier), lock the target section and read MAX + 1 under it, then section_changed — plus a conditional reordered, because an item's position is within its section, so a move must append and §8.2 binds new_display_order to reordered alone. Same conditional shape CreateMenuItemAsync already uses for description_changed.
MenuWorkflow.cs — the verb, publishing MenuChanged on Moved only.
ManageMenuItem.razor — a .manage-inline-form picker (.manage-inline-form already styles select, so no CSS moves), replacing the comment that currently says the verb does not exist.
MenuAdministrationTests (26 → ~30), MenuWiringTests (18 → 19, fake gains the verb), AdministrationJourneys.MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, and scenario 17 gains a move step at the end — moving "Apple soup" out of Starters into Puddings, where it must land after the pie, proving MAX + 1-within-target through a browser and over the §9 broadcast.
